newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan Aug money supply seen up 3.7% yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan Aug money supply seen up 3.7% yr/yr.

text.p: Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs), the key gauge of money supply, is expected to have grown 3.7 percent in August from a year earlier, economists say.

Economists polled by Reuters in Tokyo on Tuesday gave predictions of growth ranging from 3.6 percent to 3.8 percent and averaging out at about 3.7 percent. In July, money supply also grew a preliminary 3.7 percent from a year earlier.
The August money supply results should show that the nation's economy is recovering gradually, economists said. The data will be released at 11 a.m. (0200 GMT) on Wednesday.
"There should be little change overall. Economic recovery still seems gradual," said Atsushi Takeda, an economist for DKB Research Institute.
A lack of growth in bank lending is preventing the money supply from increasing, Takeda said.
"There's little growth in private-sector fund demand. Corporations which need funds are making do with their own funds, rather than borrowing money from banks," he said.
Nikko Research Center's Tetsuro Sawano said the reason the growth rate of money supply was expected to stay unchanged from July was lack of any significant rise in capital investment.
"There's not much growth in capital investment on the part of small and medium-sized firms. Large firms, on the other hand, have been using corporate bonds to finance capital spending," Sawano said.
Both of these trends have prevented bank lending from increasing, stunting money supply growth, Sawano said.
